prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Falling pressure in rising melt: An amber melt column rises through a widening dark fissure, three short pressure cues diminish upward. Avoid: Falling confinement is schematic; no gauge, valve or already formed atmospheric cloud.
2. Upwelling rock on the hot Earth: The same cracked hot Earth in shallow cutaway shows an amber plume reaching a broad dark surface fissure. Avoid: Planetary view of internal supply; no raining sky or finished water coast.
3. Gas bubbles separating from melt: Several pale-edged round gas bubbles separate within amber melt and become larger near its upper surface. Avoid: Bubbles still enclosed in liquid rock; not escaping cloud or boiling liquid water.
4. Volcanic gas plumes: Two pale feathered gas plumes escape a low dark cracked lava surface with narrow amber fissures. Avoid: Subaerial gas above lava, not underwater suspended mineral smoke.
5. A steam-rich atmosphere: A curved dark-orange Earth limb supports a thick softly layered pale atmospheric envelope. Avoid: Atmosphere convention; water vapor itself is invisible, do not claim all haze is visible steam.
6. A young basaltic crust: A broad solid dark basalt slab with fresh angular texture and only a thin amber glow beneath its edge. Avoid: One coherent new crust surface, not separated floating rafts.
7. A cracked volcanic crust: The same dark basalt slab divided by two deep branching fractures, faint amber light below. Avoid: Surface dry and subaerial; no water already running into the cracks.
8. Hot lava among solid rock: Dark fractured basalt surrounds a distinct flowing amber lava channel on one side, cooler rock on the other. Avoid: No water or rain yet; this uneven hot/cool layout continues through rain states.
9. Infrared energy escaping to space: A curved atmospheric layer over hot dark ground releases three long sparse radiation strokes upward into empty space. Avoid: Schematic invisible infrared, no literal window or transparent hole punched through atmosphere.
10. Cooler air high above the surface: A high pale atmospheric layer floats above a lower warm haze and a distant dark ground arc. Avoid: Altitude and heat contrast; no ready-made rain cloud or frost crystals.
11. A slowly cooling steam atmosphere: The same thick atmosphere over hot ground has a dimmer upper edge and faint outward radiation strokes. Avoid: Energy-loss schematic, not a new chemical atmosphere or sudden clear breathable sky.
12. Clouds of liquid droplets: One broad softly scalloped ivory droplet cloud above an open dark gap, no rainfall reaches the bottom. Avoid: Cloud of droplets, no clear ocean below and no modern blue daytime sky.
13. Rain falling through hot air: A pale cloud releases a few long separated rain streaks that fade before a narrow hot ground edge. Avoid: Do not show persistent pooled water; some drops disappear in hot air.
14. Rain returning as steam: Rain meets the established amber lava patch and becomes a broad rising white vapor plume; adjacent dark rock stays visible. Avoid: Boiling contact with falling rain is visible; no water inventory vanishes.
15. Water recycled through the sky: One vapor plume curls upward from a cropped warm patch into a small condensing cloud, a few returning rain streaks beside it. Avoid: One compact water-recycling loop, no additional water source or sea.
16. Cool rock beside the lava: The same basalt-and-lava layout emphasizes the broad dark solid patch beside a narrow glowing channel. Avoid: Coolness cannot be directly seen; contrast heat glow and retain no standing water yet.
